newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: APN says ready for continued profit growth.
newsitem.headline: APN says ready for continued profit growth.

text.p: Australian Provincial Newspapers Ltd (APN) said on Tuesday the newspaper publisher was well positioned to continue to grow profits and would focus on extracting growth from its existing businesses rather than through acquisitions.
Earlier APN reported a 12.6 percent rise in pre-abnormal net profit to A$12.6 million in the six months ended June 30, 1997.
"APN has performed well despite difficult trading conditions," APN said in a statement accompanying its results.
"The directors believe that the group is well-positioned to continue to grow profits, and will further benefit from an uplift in market conditions when they occur," it said.

It said it had grown substantially through acquisition in recent years. "While new opportunities continue to be investigated, the company's primary focus is on extracting the substantial organic growth inherent in its existing business."
APN said it received a claim of up to A$30 million from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) on assessments to some its units for the year ended December 31, 1991 to 1994.
"The possible claim relates to matters which were the subject of detailed accounting and tax advice at the time."
"The company believes the ATO claim will not be sustained and if necessary, will defend its position vigourously, having regard to further legal and tax advice received," it said.
APN is 49 percent owned by Irish media group Independent Newspapers Plc INSW.L and the family interests of Irish businessman Tony O'Reilly.
APN shares closed five cents lower at A$2.11.
